items.q: Why does Mel Robbins call happiness her hardest internal work?
items.a: Not parties or laughter — **content wherever she is**. Outer wins (marriage, money, business built mostly in the last six years) never silenced the inner drumbeat; when problems left, the **campaign of misery** turned on her.

items.q: What was the Vermont deck breakthrough?
items.a: For the first time she was **not 15 steps ahead** — "Is this what happiness is — that I'm just able to be right here without the anxiety, without the stress?" That is **happiness as present contentment** (Eckhart Tolle *Power of Now* parallel).

items.q: What is the campaign of misery?
items.a: An **active default to loss and complaint** — gripping what makes you unhappy. At USC parents weekend she caught herself gripping the coming loss instead of present gifts. When nothing is rationally wrong outside, the campaign **attacks the self**.

items.q: What does the curling-iron metaphor teach about discontent?
items.a: After burning her ear, daughter Kendall said "you got to learn somehow." Feel the **fire of discontent**, let the body absorb it, then **pull back toward calm** next time — don't wrestle thoughts alone.

items.q: How do you practice presence when the mind races ahead?
items.a: Train **nervous-system body-anchoring** (where your feet are) over thought-wrestling. Allow sadness without "fixing" it — **missing equals loving** — and reframe toward what is already good. Busyness was an outrun until the pandemic stripped it.

items.q: How does the countdown-visit mindset ruin presence?
items.a: Shetty's London family pattern: **counting days left** vs celebrating days present. Living day 1 as day 21 collapses presence into perpetual leaving.
**No middle ground** — you are either in the stands commenting/jealous/delaying or on the court playing. The pain of never leaving the stands exceeds **tripping on the court**.

items.q: Why replace "fake it till you make it"?
items.a: "Fake it" names yourself fake and **amplifies doubt**. Use **try until you make it** — get on the court and do the reps ("crappy songs daily"). The flame of potential never goes out; arguing against it via the campaign is like an **internal cancer**.

items.q: Is hustle the enemy of peace?
items.a: Robbins rejects the binary: you need **deep quiet and sprint busyness** — busyness just cannot stay the **default**. Settling for familiar stuck pain to avoid dream-pursuit pain is the **mediocrity trap** she calls the worst advice.
